title: Small Airway Dysfunction in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Systemic Sclerosis
off: Study on Small Airway Dysfunction in Rheumatoid Arthritis and Systemic Sclerosis
summary: The purpose of this prospective real-world study is to assess the presence and severity of small airway dysfunction in patients with rheumatoid arthritis or systemic sclerosis and to examine the relationships between the various markers of small airway dysfunction and disease activity.
desc:
Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a serious pulmonary complication of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic sclerosis (SSc) and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Patients with symptomatic ILD have been reported to have a two-fold to tenfold higher risk of death than those without ILD. Early identification of patients with RA or SSc who are at risk of developing progressive ILD therefore remains a major clinical challenge.

Current international recommendations advocate regular pulmonary function testing (PFT), including forced spirometry and measurement of the diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO), as well as the six-minute walk test, with chest computed tomography (CT) performed when clinically indicated, for the detection and monitoring of ILD in patients with RA or SSc. However, these conventional investigations may have limited sensitivity for detecting early pulmonary abnormalities, and PFT results may remain within the normal range during the initial stages of ILD. Recent studies have shown that small airway dysfunction (SAD) may occur early in the course of pulmonary involvement in patients with RA or SSc, even in the absence of radiological evidence of established pulmonary fibrosis.

The present descriptive study therefore aimed to characterize pulmonary abnormalities in patients with RA or SSc using a multimodal approach that combine assessment of ventilatory mechanics by impulse oscillometry (IOS), evaluation of distal airway inflammation through multiple-flow exhaled nitric oxide measurements (CANO), and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients ≥ 18 years of age
* Diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) or systemic sclerosis (SSc) confirmed by a rheumatologist
* Patients affiliated with or covered by a social security scheme
* Patients who have received information regarding the research and have signed the consent form.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Presence of interstitial lung disease (ILD) identified prior to recruitment
* History of treatment with medications known to induce pulmonary fibrosis (bleomycin, amiodarone) or prior radiation therapy for the local treatment of thoracic malignancies (breast cancer, lung cancer)
* Patients unable to perform any of the following pulmonary function tests (PFTs):

  * Impulse oscillometry (IOS)
  * Forced spirometry
  * Measurement of lung volumes via plethysmography
* Individuals covered under Articles L1121-5 to 1121-8 of the French Public Health Code (minors, adults under legal guardianship or curatorship, individuals deprived of their liberty, pregnant or breastfeeding women)
* Patients who do not understand the French language.
